parent.intent: Scales the return_distance coefficient by progress so the closing-cost signal strengthens as more cities are visited. Early steps preserve the parent's greedy locality (clustered/grid intact); late steps bias toward candidates that keep the eventual return-to-start short, addressing the uniform family where lack of cluster structure leaves closing cost underweighted. All terms remain linear and bounded; progress is in [0,1] so the added return weight stays in [0, 0.15].
parent.code:
def priority(f):
    d = f["distance"]
    rd = f["return_distance"]
    rg = f["regret"]
    pr = f["progress"]
    return -d + (0.25 + 0.15 * pr) * rd + 0.2 * rg
